subject.title: Long streaming model responses cause event loop starvation

question: Should maintainers sponsor a current-main long-output Gateway stress proof first, or treat the existing stream-yield and Gateway-throttle mitigations as sufficient without further product work?
rationale: The source shows partial mitigations, but choosing between no-op, more cooperative yielding, worker offload, or downstream Gateway projection changes depends on maintainer tolerance for performance risk and the live proof boundary.

options.title: Require current-main stress proof first
options.body: Use a live or synthetic long-output provider run to identify the remaining hotspot before opening a new fix PR or closing the report.

options.title: Close after maintainer-accepted mitigation review
options.body: Accept the existing shipped mitigations as sufficient and close only if maintainers are comfortable without a fresh end-to-end proof.

options.title: Sponsor architectural hardening
options.body: Treat long-output streaming as a known resilience gap and design a broader offload/yield/fanout strategy before implementation.

recommendation.title: Require current-main stress proof first
recommendation.body: Use a live or synthetic long-output provider run to identify the remaining hotspot before opening a new fix PR or closing the report.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest recent history across text-delta mitigation and Gateway chat timing evidence for this path.
